summary: Rs 3,000 for the tower body (rings, basin, cups, pipe, GST) is realistic only at scale. Base case: about 2,200 towers if only the ring is moulded and clusters share a tank (route g2), or about 7,900 towers with a full Indian P20 mould set (route a). At 600 towers the best own-design body costs about Rs 4,500-5,000 (base); at 200 towers about Rs 8,500-9,500. A complete, ready-to-plant tower (with pump/timer/reservoir share) costs about Rs 4,100-4,300 at 6,000 towers, against Rs 11,100 for bulk-bought kits and Rs 5,545 for DIY PVC. DIY PVC is the cheapest complete option up to about 600 towers; Indian contract injection moulding wins at 6,000. Resin is the main cost: PP injection grade rose from Rs 90.7/kg (1 Jan 2026) to Rs 154.7/kg (16 Sep 2026, IOCL ex-works Bangalore), so 8 kg of plastic now costs about Rs 1,450 before GST. Tooling: about Rs 12 lakh (ring mould + development) for the lean route, Rs 26 lakh for a full Indian P20 set, about Rs 40 lakh for a China set landed (moulds Rs 36 lakh + development). China-made parts are not cheaper at Rs 96/USD with about 38-40% duty and IGST. Owning presses pays only above about 20,000-37,000 towers a year.

definitions.body_kit_inr: Tower body the Rs 3,000 target refers to: moulded/formed parts (11 rings, basin or tray, seed holder, lid, spout) + 88 bought net cups + central pipe and fittings + 18% GST + rejects + assembly + local freight + tooling and development spread over the volume. Values are [low, base, high].
definitions.complete_inr: Body kit + pump, timer and reservoir share, so it compares with ready kits and DIY PVC. Excludes site wiring, structure and site preparation. Values are [low, base, high].
definitions.design_basis: 88 sites (11 rings x 8 pockets), 30-50 L basin per tower except g2, bought net cups, Rs 96/USD, Sep 2026 resin prices in base.
definitions.scenario_logic: Low uses every optimistic input together (early-2026 resin price, light parts, low quotes); high uses every pessimistic input. The real result will sit between them.

how_to_check: Designs: https://search.ipindia.gov.in/designsearch (fields: article name, IDC/Locarno class, applicant; data from April 1997, except 2005, 2006 and 2008; not valid for legal proceedings). Search article names such as hydroponic, planter, grow tower, aeroponic, vertical garden, and class 11-02 (flower pots).
Patents: https://iprsearch.ipindia.gov.in/PublicSearch (title, abstract, complete specification, IPC; has a CAPTCHA, so search it yourself). Also check Google Patents with country IN.

Examples found: US10136594B2 (Tower Garden LLC, aeroponic tower, expires 3 May 2036; Google Patents lists no India family member) and US10729080B2 (expires 2038; US only). Foreign patents do not bind in India but matter if towers are exported.
ip_notes.design_around: Registered designs protect appearance only. Change the pocket shape, ring profile, rib pattern and surface features so the ring does not look like any registered design; keep only functional features that are not patented in India. Do not copy the purchased tower CAD one-to-one; measure it for fit and function only.

risks: Resin price: IOCL PP injection grade rose about 70% in 2026 (Rs 90.7 to Rs 154.7/kg, Jan-Sep) after the West Asia conflict; material is about 85-90% of moulded-part cost. A Rs 30/kg move changes the body cost by about Rs 300 per tower incl. GST.
Volume risk: tooling only pays at thousands of towers. Earlier Floruvi demand research advised starting with 60-150 towers; 6,000 towers is not yet supported by demand.

Design risk: 8 angled pockets per ring are undercuts that need side actions; thin rings warp; an 11-ring stack must carry wet plants and wind load; UV life depends on HALS dose and wall thickness. Budget 2-3 mould trials (T1-T3).
Basin needs a 600-800 t press; few moulders have one free and the mould is costly. Avoid by buying a tub or using a shared cluster tank.

Toolmaker quality: very low Indian quotes may use unhardened or non-certified steel and poor cooling (long cycles, warpage). China moulds may not fit Indian presses (tie-bar spacing, locating ring, ejector layout, 415 V hot-runner controllers) and design files can leak.

China parts: at Rs 96/USD, BCD 15% + SWS (+AIDC) + 18% IGST (about 38-40%) and freight make parts dearer than Indian moulding; MOQs of 500-5,000 pieces; customs classification disputes; slow replacement of broken parts.
GST: 18% on parts and moulds is not recoverable for a farm that sells exempt fresh produce.
Food safety and claims: food-contact PP/HDPE and masterbatches need declarations; IS 9845 migration testing per material/colour; no published INR price found.

IP: copying the exact look of a registered Indian design is piracy under Designs Act s.22 (up to Rs 50,000 per design, or damages and injunction); functional features may be patented. The IP India design and patent search pages need a manual (CAPTCHA) search that was not done here.

Owning machines: a 250 t press breaks even only at about 3,500-6,500 machine-hours a year (about 20,000-37,000 towers); a basin press would idle most of the year. Big presses also need HT power, a hoist and skilled setters.
Cluster pumping: one pump failure or root disease can affect 10-20 towers; keep a standby pump and alarms (earlier Floruvi research).
Estimate uncertainty: many tooling and conversion numbers are estimates from listing prices; get at least 3 written quotes before committing.
recommendations: For the first 200 towers, do not buy moulds. Build DIY PVC towers (IS 4985 lead-free) or negotiate bulk kit prices, and use this phase to prove demand and the tower design.

If you make your own design, mould only the part that defines the tower: the ring panel (route g/g2). Buy net cups (Rs 2-4.5), use a bought tub or a shared cluster tank, and use standard pipe, spray heads and fittings.

Design the ring for a 250-350 t press: 2.0-2.5 mm walls with ribs, target 0.35-0.40 kg per ring, and a panel layout that needs few or no side actions. Ask the toolmaker for a free DFM and mould-flow report before cutting steel.
Use P20 steel (not H13) for 1,000+ towers; use an aluminium ring mould (about Rs 1.5-7 lakh) if you want 200-600 towers of your own design with low risk.

Get written quotes from 3 Indian toolrooms (Peenya/Bommasandra, Pune, Rajkot/Ahmedabad) and 2 China toolmakers. Require the steel certificate, cooling layout, shot-life guarantee, T1 samples, mould ownership, spare inserts, and staged payment (for example 40/40/20).
Choose PP impact copolymer or HDPE injection grade with 1-2% HALS UV masterbatch and white masterbatch; get food-contact declarations and one IS 9845 migration test per material and colour.
Put a resin price-variation clause (linked to IOCL/RIL lists) in the moulding contract; buy resin forward only if prices fall back towards early-2026 levels.
Contract-mould; do not buy presses below about 20,000 towers a year or without other products to fill the machine.

Before tooling, pay a patent agent for a novelty search (Rs 15,000-30,000) and an FTO opinion; search IP India designs by article name (hydroponic, planter, grow tower, aeroponic) and class 11-02 (flower pots). Change the appearance of any registered design you find; consider registering your own ring design.
Treat 18% GST as a cost in every budget unless Floruvi registers and sells towers.
